lines.japanese: 「委員長、ちょっとこーい」
lines.english: “Class rep, get over here a second.”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 昼休み。学食にパンを買いに行こうと思った矢先、高内さんから声をかけられた。困ったな、早く行かないとすぐなくなっちゃうのに。
lines.english: Lunch break. Just as I was about to go buy bread at the cafeteria, Takauchi called me over. This was a problem. If I did not hurry, it would all sell out.

lines.japanese: 「なに」
lines.english: “What is it?”

lines.japanese: だけど無視するわけにもいかないし、僕は高内さんの机まで向かった。できれば二言三言で終わってくれるといいな。
lines.english: But I could hardly ignore her, so I went to Takauchi’s desk. I hoped we could settle the matter in two or three sentences.

lines.japanese: 「悪りいんだけどさ、文集のコレ、出席番号順にまとめといてくんない」
lines.english: “Sorry, but could you put these anthology pages in student-number order?”

lines.japanese: 高内さんの机に、クリップで束ねられた原稿用紙がばさりと落ちた。一目見て、とても昼休み中に捌ききれるような量じゃない。しかも──
lines.english: A sheaf of manuscript paper held together by a clip landed on Takauchi’s desk. One glance told me there was far too much to finish over lunch. And besides—

lines.japanese: 「──この仕事って、こないだ決めた分担で、高内さんたちの班がやるはずじゃ……」
lines.english: “—under the assignments we decided the other day, wasn’t your group supposed to do this?”

lines.japanese: 「そーね、うん。だから頼んでンだけど。分かんなかった？」
lines.english: “Yep. Exactly. That’s why I’m asking you. Was that unclear?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 彼女はぐいと原稿用紙を押しつけてきた。机から落ちそうだったので、思わず受けとめてしまった。
lines.english: She shoved the manuscript pages toward me. They nearly fell from the desk, and I caught them without thinking.

lines.japanese: 「ね、いーでしょ、頼むよ羽田ぁ。これやってくれたらさ、おまえが前に放課後の約束ブッチした件も、貸し借りゼロでチャラになんじゃん。な？　いいだろ？」
lines.english: “Come on, Haneda, do me a favor. If you do this, we’ll call it square over that time you ditched our plans after school. No debts either way. Yeah? Fair enough, right?”

lines.japanese: 高内さんにぱんと尻を叩かれた。痛くはなかったけど、その瞬間に、原稿用紙が重くなった気がした。
lines.english: Takauchi gave me a brisk slap on the rear. It did not hurt, but at that instant the manuscript seemed to grow heavier.

lines.japanese: 「ん、えっと……」
lines.english: “Mm, well...”
“All right...”

lines.japanese: 「分かったよ」
lines.english: “I’ll do it.”

lines.japanese: 「いっや、さすがは委員長！　じゃ、私これから昼メシ行くからヨロ～」
lines.english: “I knew we could count on the class rep! I’m heading to lunch, so I’ll leave it to you!”

lines.japanese: 高内さんは財布を鞄から取りだすと、いつも一緒にいる友人ふたりの元へ駆けていってしまった。
lines.english: Takauchi pulled her wallet from her bag and ran off to join the two friends she was always with.

lines.japanese: 僕は逆に財布をしまうと、机に原稿用紙をばさりと置いた。僕の机に腰掛けていた鴻野君が、唸りながらお尻をどけて作業スペースを空けてくれた。
lines.english: I put my own wallet away and dropped the manuscript on my desk. Kono, who had been sitting there, groaned and shifted his backside out of the way to clear me some space.

lines.japanese: 分厚い原稿用紙を束ねるクリップを外し、一枚ずつ意味もなくめくっていく。何をしたいのか分からないけど、何もしないで座っているところをクラスのみんなに見られたくなかったんだと思う。
lines.english: I removed the clip from the thick sheaf and turned the pages one by one for no reason at all. I did not know what I was trying to accomplish. Perhaps I simply did not want the class to see me sitting there doing nothing.

lines.japanese: 一番最後のページに辿りついたとき、いつか食べた野菜サンドの味をふと思いだした。苦手なキュウリが青臭くて辛かったなあ。
lines.english: When I reached the final page, I suddenly remembered the taste of a vegetable sandwich I had eaten once. I hated cucumber; its raw, grassy taste had been hard to stomach.

lines.japanese: もう一度、最初のページに戻る。そしてまた、ぱらぱらを始める。やっぱり何をしてるのか、自分でも分からない。でもこの無意味な作業を止めることが相当の苦痛であることは分かっていた。
lines.english: I returned to the first page and began flipping through them again. I still had no idea what I was doing. But I knew it would be remarkably painful to stop this meaningless motion.

lines.japanese: 三度目のぱらぱらに取りかかりながら、なんとなく高内さんのことを考えた。いまごろ学食でメニューを選んでるのだろうか。
lines.english: As I began a third pass, my thoughts drifted to Takauchi. Perhaps she was choosing her meal in the cafeteria now.

lines.japanese: うん、高内さんが昼食を抜いてお腹を空かせるよりいいじゃないか。いつだって僕は誰かの力になりたいんだ。さっさと済ませてしまおう。
lines.english: Yes. Wasn’t this better than Takauchi going hungry without lunch? I always wanted to be useful to someone. I would finish it quickly.

lines.japanese: 僕は手を止めた。原稿用紙を起こして、机の上でとんとん下辺を揃える。よし、やるぞ──
lines.english: I stopped flipping through the pages, stood them upright, and tapped their bottom edges square against the desk. All right. Time to begin—

lines.japanese: 「終わった？」
lines.english: “Finished?”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 気合いを入れて制服の袖をまくったら、渡来さんが現れた。
lines.english: Just as I rolled up my uniform sleeves with determination, Watarai appeared.

lines.japanese: 手を後ろに回してそわそわ揺れてる。なんだろう、普段より落ちつきがないように見えるけど──
lines.english: She held her hands behind her back and rocked restlessly. What was it? She seemed less composed than usual—

lines.japanese: ──なんて考えていたら、彼女の方が先に口を開いた。
lines.english: —while I wondered, she spoke first.

lines.japanese: 「なんか高内と話してたみたいだけど、用事はもう済んだの？」
lines.english: “You looked like you were talking to Takauchi. Are you finished with whatever it was?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、済んだっていうか、むしろ作業はこれからだけど……え、なに、おれに用？」
lines.english: “Finished? If anything, the work is only beginning... Why? Did you need me?”

lines.japanese: 思わず訊いてしまった。気付いたら渡来さんが何やら難しい顔をしている。
lines.english: The question slipped out. Before I knew it, Watarai had assumed a grave expression.

lines.japanese: しかし彼女は僕の問いに答えなかった。というか僕の話など聞いていない感じ。後ろに回していた手を解いたと思ったら、ずいっと目の前になにかを突きだしてきた。
lines.english: But she did not answer. In fact, she hardly seemed to have heard me. She brought her hands out from behind her back and thrust something abruptly in front of me.

lines.japanese: 「これ」
lines.english: “This.”

lines.japanese: 眉間に皺を寄せたような硬い表情。渡来さんはなぜか怒ってるみたいだった。少なくとも僕には、彼女を不快にさせた心当たりはない。
lines.english: Her expression was stiff, her brow drawn tight. For some reason, Watarai looked angry. I could think of nothing I had done to offend her.

lines.japanese: 「これ？　これなに？」
lines.english: “This? What is it?”

lines.japanese: 黄色い布に包まれた直方体からは、温かい空気と、空腹の体には堪えられない香りが漂ってきた。
lines.english: The rectangular object wrapped in yellow cloth radiated warmth and a fragrance almost unbearable on an empty stomach.

lines.japanese: 「彼氏におべんと作ってきた」
lines.english: “I made lunch for my boyfriend.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんが俺に？　はい？　なに？
lines.english: Watarai had made it for me? What? Excuse me?

lines.japanese: 「え、なんで──」
lines.english: “Why would you—”

lines.japanese: 「なんでって、だってうちら彼氏彼女じゃん。弁当ぐらい当たり前でしょ」
lines.english: “What do you mean, why? We’re boyfriend and girlfriend. Making you lunch is perfectly normal.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは無言でナプキン包みをぐいぐいと押しだしてくる。受けとれってことらしい。
lines.english: Without another word, Watarai pushed the napkin-wrapped box insistently toward me. Apparently I was to take it.

lines.japanese: 嬉しい。すごく嬉しい。でも彼女の表情は明らかに普通じゃない。なんなんだろう、この状況は。なにか含みがあるのか。本当に受けとっていいのだろうか。
lines.english: I was happy. Overwhelmingly happy. Yet her expression was plainly not normal. What was happening here? Was there some catch? Could I really accept it?

lines.japanese: 「あの、なんで怒ってるの」
lines.english: “Um... Why are you angry?”

lines.japanese: 「は？　べつに怒ってはいないよ」
lines.english: “What? I’m not angry.”

lines.japanese: 顔も声も不機嫌としか思えない。なんだろう。僕は気付かないところで失態を犯していたんだろうか。
lines.english: Her face and voice could mean nothing but displeasure. What had happened? Had I committed some offense without realizing it?

lines.japanese: 僕がいつまでも受けとらずにいると、周囲からひそひそとした声が聞こえてきた。いま気がついたけど、さっきまでざわついていたのに、今はほとんど雑談の声が聞こえない。
lines.english: As I stood there without taking the box, whispers rose around us. Only then did I notice that the classroom, noisy moments ago, had lost nearly all its idle chatter.

lines.japanese: 代わりに、ひそひそと声を潜めた音量で僕の名前が聞こえてきた。合間合間に渡来さんの名前。
lines.english: Instead, I heard my name among the lowered voices, with Watarai’s threaded between.

lines.japanese: もしかして僕はいま教室中の視線を集めているんじゃないだろうか。そう考えると恥ずかしい。
lines.english: Could every eye in the classroom be fixed on me? The thought was embarrassing.

lines.japanese: 気が付くと渡来さんの頬もほんのり朱に染まっていた。怒った顔のまま赤くなっている渡来さんは、それはそれで可愛いと思ってしまった。
lines.english: When I looked again, Watarai’s cheeks had taken on the faintest red. I found that angry, blushing face adorable in its own way.

lines.japanese: 「なに？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いや……どうしたらいいのかと思って」
lines.english: “Nothing... I was wondering what I should do.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだと。受けとらないってことは、いらないってことか」
lines.english: “What was that? If you won’t take it, does that mean you don’t want it?”

lines.japanese: 「や、欲しい……けど、え、じゃあこれ、もらってもいいの？」
lines.english: “No, I want it... But—may I really have it?”

lines.japanese: 「いいよ？」
lines.english: “Of course.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、ありがとう、でもなんで怒って……」
lines.english: “Then thank you. But why are you angry...?”

lines.japanese: 「怒ってないってば。いいから──」
lines.english: “I told you I’m not angry. Just—”

lines.japanese: 「──は、恥ずかしいんだから、早く受けとってよ！」
lines.english: “—i-it’s embarrassing, so hurry up and take it!”

lines.japanese: 「あっ」
lines.english: “Oh.”

lines.japanese: 僕は慌てて手を伸ばした。ずしん。思ってたより重量がある。
lines.english: I hurriedly reached for it. A solid weight settled into my hands. It was heavier than I had expected.

lines.japanese: でも渡来さんはいま恥ずかしいと言った。
lines.english: But Watarai had just said she was embarrassed.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうか。なんだ。渡来さん、怒ってたんじゃなくて──」
lines.english: “Oh, I see. So you weren’t angry—”

lines.japanese: 「──照れてたんだ」
lines.english: “—you were embarrassed.”

lines.japanese: なるほど、渡来さんって、照れると怒ってるみたいになるんだ。
lines.english: I understood. When Watarai was embarrassed, she looked angry.

lines.japanese: 「うるさい」
lines.english: “Shut up.”

lines.japanese: 真っ赤な顔で睨まれた。
lines.english: She glared at me, her face crimson.

lines.japanese: 「そーゆーこと、気付いても言わないでよ」
lines.english: “Even if you notice something like that, don’t say it out loud.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうだね。ごめん。でも良かった、渡来さんが怒ってるわけじゃなくて」
lines.english: “Oh. Right. I’m sorry. But I’m glad you weren’t angry.”

lines.japanese: 「ふぅー！」
lines.english: “Phewwww!”

lines.japanese: 彼女がとつぜん大きく息を吹いた。そのあとには、肩の力が抜けたみたいに表情が柔らかくなっていた。
lines.english: She abruptly released a great breath. Afterward, the tension seemed to leave her shoulders, and her expression softened.

lines.japanese: 「あー緊張した」
lines.english: “God, that was nerve-racking.”

lines.japanese: 口調も角が取れてる。
lines.english: The sharpness had left her voice too.

lines.japanese: 「こんな恥ずかしいなら、やっぱり持ってこなきゃよかったよ」
lines.english: “If I’d known it would be this embarrassing, I never would’ve brought it.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「私、本番に弱いタイプだから。逆に言うと舞台立つまでは、ことの大きさに気付けないのかも」
lines.english: “I’m the kind who falls apart when the moment actually comes. Or maybe I don’t understand how big a thing is until I’m standing onstage.”

lines.japanese: しばしば渡来さんって、行間を読まなきゃ伝わらない文脈で会話したがるよなあ。
lines.english: Watarai often spoke as though you had to read between the lines just to follow her.

lines.japanese: 「どういうこと？」
lines.english: “What do you mean?”

lines.japanese: 「ほら、私って羽田君に貸しイチあったでしょ」
lines.english: “Remember, I owed you one.”

lines.japanese: 「で、こないだ羽田君がお昼はパン食派だって言ってたから。じゃあ自分の作るついでに持ってってやるかあって思って。うん、そんだけ」
lines.english: “And the other day you said you usually had bread for lunch. So I thought, if I’m making mine anyway, I might as well bring you one too. That’s all.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、クラスのみんなの手前じゃ彼氏彼女なんだし、おべんと渡すぐらい普通じゃんとか思ってたんだけど……難しいね。あー恥ずかし。もう二度と持ってこない」
lines.english: “I thought, well, in front of everyone we’re boyfriend and girlfriend, so giving you lunch should be perfectly normal... But it’s hard. God, how embarrassing. I’m never bringing one again.”

lines.japanese: 「ま、食べよう羽田君」
lines.english: “Well, let’s eat, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “All right.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は僕の前の椅子を回転させると、優雅な動作ですとんと腰を下ろした。
lines.english: She turned the chair in front of mine around and settled gracefully into it.

lines.japanese: 彼女が無言で包みを開けたので、僕もそれに倣ってみる。中にはお弁当に入れる代名詞的なおかずが綺麗に並んでいた。
lines.english: She silently untied her wrapping, and I followed suit. Inside, all the classic staples of a boxed lunch were arranged beautifully.

lines.japanese: 僕も羽田の家ではちょっとしたものを作ることがあるので、渡来さんの腕のほどは知れた。
lines.english: I sometimes made simple things at the Haneda house myself, so I could tell how skilled Watarai was.

lines.japanese: 「へえ、渡来さん料理上手だったんだ」
lines.english: “I didn’t know you were such a good cook.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだ、地球温暖化の話でもしよっか」
lines.english: “Oh, I know—want to talk about global warming?”

lines.japanese: 「え、どうしてそんなあからさまに話題を変えるの？」
lines.english: “Why would you change the subject that blatantly?”

lines.japanese: 「や、や、や、だって、恥ずかしいじゃん……」
lines.english: “B-b-because it’s embarrassing...”

lines.japanese: 「なんで。せっかく渡来さんの料理が上手なんだから、その話をしようよ」
lines.english: “Why? You’re an excellent cook, so let’s talk about that.”

lines.japanese: 「お願い、許してください。もう食べなくていいから」
lines.english: “Please. Have mercy. You don’t even have to eat it anymore.”

lines.japanese: 「なんで。食べるよ。そんなこと言わないでよ。せっかく作ってくれたのに、渡来さんのお弁当食べたいよ」
lines.english: “Why would you say that? Of course I’ll eat it. You went to the trouble of making it, and I want to eat the lunch you made.”

lines.japanese: 「……ありがと」
lines.english: “...Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 「ほら、この卵焼きなんておいしいなあ。おれ、こういうの大好きだよ」
lines.english: “Look, this rolled omelet is delicious. I love this kind.”

lines.japanese: 「……よかった、作ってきて」
lines.english: “...I’m glad I made it.”

lines.japanese: 食事中、ふと達成済みの残務処理“２：学食のチキンソテー＆エビフライ定食を食べる”を思いだして、急にその一文が恥ずかしくなった。
lines.english: During the meal, I suddenly remembered a completed item on my list of unfinished business: ‘2: Eat the chicken sauté and fried-shrimp set meal in the cafeteria.’ All at once, the sentence mortified me.

lines.japanese: 今日は三年間のうちで一番上等な昼ごはんだったってことを、文句なしに断言しておこう。
lines.english: Let the record show, without qualification, that this was the finest lunch of my three years at school.

lines.japanese: やっぱり与えられた作業は昼休みだけじゃ終わらず、放課後になってからも続いていた。
lines.english: As expected, the work I had been given did not end with lunch. It continued after school.

lines.japanese: ただ、それは必ずしも苦行だとは言いきれない。なぜなら、いまの僕には強力な味方がいるからだ。
lines.english: Yet I could not quite call it an ordeal. I now had a powerful ally.

lines.japanese: 「こりゃー。ひとにだけやらせて、何さぼっとるー」
lines.english: “Hey! You make me do all the work while you sit there slacking off?”

lines.japanese: 「さぼってないよ、ちょっと考えごとしてただけだってば」
lines.english: “I’m not slacking. I was just thinking for a minute.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、それをさぼってたって言うよね。羽田君、亭主関白のひとかもね」
lines.english: “Yes, that’s what people call slacking. Maybe you’re the kind of husband who expects to rule the roost, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「どうだろう。でもこの現状はむしろ、かかあ天下だよ」
lines.english: “I don’t know. Right now, I’d say the wife rules the roost.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだと」
lines.english: “What was that?”

lines.japanese: 「ご、ごめんなさい。ちょっとさぼってました」
lines.english: “I-I’m sorry. I was slacking a little.”

lines.japanese: 「うん。で、なに考えてたの？」
lines.english: “Good. So what were you thinking about?”

lines.japanese: 「なにって、渡来さんのこととか」
lines.english: “About you, for one.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「だっておれは、卒文制作の作業をぜんぶ自分ひとりでやることになりそうで絶望してたんだ。だからいま渡来さんがいてくれること、本当に感謝してる」
lines.english: “I was in despair because it looked as though I would have to make the entire graduation anthology alone. So I’m truly grateful you’re here now.”

lines.japanese: 僕はちょっと照れくさかったから、渡来さんの顔を見ずに作業に集中するふりをした。
lines.english: A little embarrassed, I pretended to concentrate on the work rather than look at Watarai’s face.

lines.japanese: だけど渡来さんは、そんな僕をわざわざ顔を横に倒して覗きこんできた。
lines.english: But Watarai went out of her way to tilt her head sideways and peer up at me.

lines.japanese: 「だって私から羽田君の班に入れてもらったんだもん。当然だよ」
lines.english: “I’m the one who asked you to let me join your group. Of course I’m here.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことないよ。渡来さんが入ってくれて嬉しかったよ」
lines.english: “That doesn’t make it a given. I was happy when you joined.”

lines.japanese: 「嬉しい……」
lines.english: “Happy...”

lines.japanese: 彼女の口の端が、緩やかに曲線を描いていく。
lines.english: The corner of her mouth slowly traced a curve.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、班員は多い方がいいもんね。ひとりでも多い方が嬉しいよね、それは」
lines.english: “Oh. Of course you’d be happier with more people in the group. Anyone would be glad to have one extra member.”
